handoff_instructions.purpose: Handoffs document the current state and scope of the project so a new LLM session can pick up exactly where the last one left off. They are the primary continuity mechanism for this project.
what_to_include: A summary of what was done, discussed, decided, or built in this session
What worked and what did not work
Current pipeline state — what scripts exist, what their status is, what the next steps are
A condensed recap of prior sessions so the new LLM has full project context without reading every previous handoff
Open questions or blockers that carry into the next session
what_not_to_include: Exhaustive code listings — reference file paths instead
Decisions that were reversed or abandoned mid-session — only document final state
Speculation about distant future work — stay close to what is actually next
format_rules: This handoff_instructions block must appear at the top of every future handoff
When a user says 'create a handoff for this session,' use this block as the template and fill in the session-specific fields
Prior session summaries should be condensed — one paragraph per session, not a full retelling
Be brief but complete. A new LLM should be able to start working immediately after reading this file

what_was_done_this_session.road_LF_wired_to_centerline: ROOT CAUSE found for road_LF=null: build sourced road_LF ONLY from parsed station-label text (raw.road_alignments), which was empty for Woodman — while the road centerline polyline length sat UNUSED in raw.linear_features. Fix made in phase1/ingest/build_case_library.py: new module helpers _is_centerline_layer() + _road_lf_from_dwg(). road_LF now = sum of length on road-centerline layers (layer name contains 'ROAD' AND a token in {CNTR, CENTERLINE, -CL, ALGN, ALIGN}), preferred; station-label parse is fallback; null if no extraction. New field derived.scale_metrics.road_LF_source records provenance ('dwg_centerline:<layer>', 'dwg_station_labels', or null). Per-job summary print updated to show it.

what_was_done_this_session.diagnostic_written_then_obviated: phase1/ingest/diag_dwg_coverage.py — read-only auditor that reports per-layer TOP-LEVEL vs NESTED(inside xrefs/blocks) length to quantify what py1 misses. Was built to test an xref hypothesis; became unnecessary once Nolan reconciled the DWG version (centerline is top-level C-ROAD-CNTR, not nested). Keep as an audit tool or delete.

key_findings_and_decisions: THE CENTERLINE WAS NOT BEING FILTERED OR LOST. is_proposed_layer() only drops layers containing -EXST-/-EXIST-/EXISTING; C-ROAD-CNTR passes. It was captured fine (937.5 ft, single LWPOLYLINE, n=1). The only defect was that build never PROMOTED it to the road_LF scale metric. So this was a wiring gap, not an extraction gap.

py1 LIMITATION (real, but deferred): py1_dwg_extract.py walks MODEL-SPACE TOP-LEVEL entities only — it does NOT descend into XREFs or block-definition inserts. Any proposed-layer geometry nested inside an xref/block is invisible. Did not bite Woodman (centerline is top-level). This is 'Fix B' — broaden traversal to virtual_entities of INSERTs — PARKED until a job actually needs it. diag_dwg_coverage.py can quantify the miss per job.

WOODMAN IS THE TRUSTED DWG REFERENCE. Its C-BASE extraction is clean. Painted Rock's extraction is BAD: it has NO road/centerline linear layers at all (road_LF=2641.3 came from station labels only), consistent with its previously-noted bad LLM qty sheet. Painted Rock must be RE-EXTRACTED; do not trust its DWG numbers until then.

ROAD CENTERLINE LAYER NAMING VARIES by firm/NCS revision (saw C-ROAD-CNTR in Woodman BASE; Nolan saw C-ROAD-ALGN-LINE in a newer/other Woodman file before reconciling versions). The matcher token set may not catch every firm — road_LF_source is the manual gate to catch misses per job.

LOT_COUNT path decided: NOT extractable from DWG basemap geometry (lots live on the plat). Will be counted by a VISION MODEL off plan/plat images (or hand-entered into the manifest). Kept entirely out of the DWG pipeline; scale_metrics.lot_count stays null for now.

next_steps: 1. PERSIST road_LF: run `python phase1/ingest/build_case_library.py` (no --dry-run) to refresh the 8 records so Woodman gets road_LF=937.5. (Dry-run already eyeballed.)

2. DWG EXTRACTION, ONE JOB AT A TIME (the main effort). For each of the 6 un-extracted jobs (and a re-extract of Painted Rock): run py1 using the per-job commands in phase1/ingest/README.md, then COMPARE the extraction output against what we already have to confirm completeness. Compare against: (a) proposal line-item quantities + the qty sheet (as-bid truth), (b) plan-sheet stationing for road_LF, (c) Woodman's clean extraction as the shape reference. Per-job because DWG file layouts and layer naming vary (root / nested 'CAD FILES' / test_copies; C-ROAD-CNTR vs C-ROAD-ALGN-LINE vs ...).

3. PER JOB, CHECK FOR THE KNOWN FAILURE MODES: road_LF_source fell back to dwg_station_labels or matched an unexpected layer (centerline missed -> maybe widen matcher tokens); curb ~3x over (parallel curb lines on one layer); anonymous dynamic-block *U### explosion inflating structure counts; multi-file double-count if BASE+DESIGN+TOPO merged; geometry hiding inside xrefs/blocks (run diag_dwg_coverage.py to quantify -> may trigger Fix B). Decide each miss: cheap matcher/layer tweak vs real extraction defect.
4. After extractions are trustworthy per job, rebuild to fold road_LF (and any other reliable scale metrics) across the library. Then proceed to M2.

6. M2 — Knowledge pack (after coverage is good): $/unit distributions (segmented by job type/region/date, recency-weighted), typical-section defaults, job-type signatures, derivation rules. Exit: a reviewable patterns doc.

prior_sessions_summary.2026_6_2.5_M1_case_library_ingest: Defined the case-library schema and built the M1 ingest: parse_proposal.py (rendered Word field = cost truth; raw =N formula can be stale; OPTIONAL items excluded from grand total; identity comes from manifest not header), parse_qty_sheet.py (clean qty_tbl_*.txt -> rows + ROW_SF/stripping; .xlsx left unparsed by design), normalize_dwg.py (extraction.json -> normalized items, positive-match-only), build_case_library.py (orchestrator). Canonical job total = total_reconciled (sum of line items); 7/8 foot to the penny, Settlement Mountain diverges by +143,900 (unitemized markup). Established DWG is unreliable for counts/curb (anonymous dynamic-block explosion, curb 3x, multi-file double-count) so it is tertiary; proposals+qty sheets are the spine. DWGs now local for all 8 jobs. Manifest holds non-derivable identity facts.
prior_sessions_summary.2026_6_2.4_phase1_kickoff: Wrote the PRD. TWO-SYSTEM architecture (A = offline knowledge build into case library + knowledge pack; B = runtime single-sheet inference by analogy + pattern gap-fill). 'Learning' = persist data + retrieve into context (RAG/in-context), NO model training. Output = line items + total + confidence band + provenance; target 10-15% of historical total. RAG deferred (~50 jobs). Job NAME is the stable key; Foundry excluded.
prior_sessions_summary.phase0_arc: Phase 0 = plan files -> HeavyBid quantity sheet (quantities only). Built a blind firm-agnostic DWG extractor (py1) + Claude qty-sheet generator (py4); validated on Woodman. Plan PDFs are fully rasterized so DWG is the geometry path. Typical-section facts (ROW width, stripping depth, paving) are hardest to extract from geometry. Detail: _handoffs/phase0_qty_sheet_generation/2026_6_2.FINAL_summary_handoff.json.
prior_sessions_summary.phase0_to_phase1_bridge: Phase 0's premise that DWG extraction is the trustworthy spine does NOT carry to Phase 1: past jobs already have finished proposals (as-bid quantities + prices), so Phase 1's spine is proposals + qty sheets and DWG shrinks to scale metrics + cross-check. This is why DWG extraction defects do not block M1.
